reasons.opus: Both involve receptivity to ideas and feelings. Permeability is about letting others' influence seep into one's thinking and mood, while Big Five openness is about curiosity, aesthetic sensitivity and seeking novelty; each can exist without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve receptiveness to outside views, but permeable is passive absorption of ideas and feelings including mood, while open-minded is deliberate weighing and fair evaluation of opposing views.
reasons.opus: Both involve letting outside views in. Permeable is passive absorption of ideas and feelings into thought and mood, while open-minded is deliberate evaluation of opposing arguments, so each has a part the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Permeable is about outside ideas and feelings seeping into one's own thinking and mood, while HEXACO openness is about aesthetic absorption, curiosity, imagination and attraction to unusual ideas; they share receptiveness to ideas but each adds something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both involve receptiveness to ideas. Permeable means being porous to other people's opinions and feelings. HEXACO openness is aesthetic, intellectual and imaginative curiosity, so each has something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Permeable is about one's own thinking and mood being easily influenced by outside input, while inclusive is about deliberately representing diverse groups and viewpoints; they share some openness to others' views but differ in focus and mechanism.

Both involve tolerance of others' behavior without restriction, but 'loose' is a broader cultural orientation covering weak norms, ambiguity and impulsivity, while 'permitting' is specifically about not objecting or interfering.

Both involve non-interference and leaving things be, but permitting is about not restricting others' choices, whereas world-accepting is a broader acceptance of the world and nature with a value on harmony.

Both involve letting others act as they wish without restriction, but the other is a specific parenting style that adds low demands and a resource role, while the target is a general non-interference trait.

Both involve going easy rather than restricting, but permitting is about non-interference with others' choices, while lenient is about low standards and comforting rather than pushing; each adds something the other lacks.

reasons.opus: Both describe deliberately harming others and enjoying it. Pernicious adds quiet, spreading damage and actual ruin, so it differs in emphasis rather than in concept.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve harming others, but the target requires deliberate malice and satisfaction in ruin, while the other covers harm by design or by chance without necessarily involving malice.

reasons.opus: Both describe malice that actively works harm on others. Pernicious adds quiet, insidious spreading of damage and satisfaction in the ruin, while malevolent stresses underlying hostility and wishing ill, so the core is shared but each adds its own emphasis.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve causing damage to others, but pernicious requires deliberate malice and satisfaction in ruin, while harmful covers indifference, negligence or incidental damage without malice.
Both involve malicious, harm-doing intent and pleasure in others' suffering, but 'evil' is broader (moral wrongness, corrupting others) while 'pernicious' stresses quiet, deliberate damage.
reasons.opus: Both describe malicious, deliberate harm taken with satisfaction in others' suffering. Pernicious is a narrower, quieter, damage-spreading form of the broader moral evil, so they differ mainly in scope.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve malicious harm to others, but pernicious is quiet, deliberate damage with satisfaction in ruin, while spiteful is specifically self-costly sabotage to deny a rival; they share a malicious core, but neither implies the other.

Both involve deliberate, covert harm to others without regard for them, but pernicious centers on malice and delight in ruin, while Machiavellian centers on strategic, self-serving manipulation and flattery, not necessarily malicious.

Both involve insistence on exact detail and high standards, but pernickety stresses fussy, hard-to-please nitpicking over minor points, while perfectionist stresses flawless, thorough quality without implying fussiness toward others.
reasons.opus: Both are about exacting standards and attention to detail, but pernickety stresses fussing over trivia and being hard to please, while perfectionist stresses flawless, complete high standards overall; each has an emphasis the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve excessive attention to minor details, but pernickety stresses fussy, hard-to-please standards about how things are done, while pedantic stresses technicalities, formal rules, and missing the main point.
reasons.opus: Both centre on excessive fussing over minor details, but pedantic stresses technicalities and formal rules at the expense of the main point, while pernickety stresses being hard to please about how things are done.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve close attention to minor details, but pernickety adds fussiness and being hard to please, while detail-oriented is about thoroughness and distrust of glossing over specifics without the fussy, demanding tone.
reasons.opus: Both centre on close attention to small details. Pernickety adds fussiness and being hard to please, while this detail-oriented adds scrutinising fine print and distrusting generalisations.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve close attention to detail, but pernickety adds fussiness and being hard to please over trivial points, while meticulous is neutral or positive carefulness and thoroughness without the fussy, critical edge.
reasons.opus: Both centre on attention to small details, but pernickety adds fussiness and being hard to please, while meticulous is careful, methodical thoroughness in one's own work without the fussing.

reasons.opus: Both centre on fussing that small things be done properly. Uptight adds tension, inability to relax and putting others on edge, while pernickety is about exacting fastidiousness that need not involve tension.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve fixation on small details and standards, but pernickety is a fussy perfectionism about getting things right, while micromanaging is controlling delegated work through hovering and dictating; neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve fussing over details and being hard to please. Micromanaging adds controlling oversight of others' delegated work, and a pernickety person need not supervise anyone, so the two overlap without either implying the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve being hard to please about standards, but pernickety is about fussing over minor details generally, while this fastidious is specifically about cleanliness and revulsion at dirt.

reasons.opus: Both involve missed deadlines, but chronic lateness is about timing and backlog, while carelessness is about sloppy, inattentive work and neglect; each can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve tasks done late, but 'perpetually behind' is chronic lateness and overload, while 'foot-dragging' is passive-aggressive stalling driven by resentment; each can occur without the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve lateness, but perpetually behind is chronic overload or disorganization, while foot-dragging is passive-aggressive resistance to requests, a different underlying concept.

reasons.opus: Both involve rushing, but one comes from an overfull schedule and the other from a disposition to treat everything as urgent, so each can occur without the other.

reasons.opus: Both leave others unable to understand one's reasoning, but perplexing is about confusing words and actions, while opaque is about deliberately withholding information, and either can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both can leave others confused, but perplexing is about baffling others in general, while incoherent is specifically about self-contradictory, untested beliefs; neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve sticking to goals, but the target stresses persistence through setbacks with flexible methods, while self-disciplined stresses resisting immediate temptation; each lacks the other's key element.

reasons.opus: Both involve adjusting methods to circumstances, but the target centres on unwavering pursuit of a goal, while flexible centres on accepting imperfect conditions and has no element of persistence.

reasons.opus: Both centre on overreacting to minor slights, but pettish is childish sulking and lingering peevishness, while petty is making disproportionate issues out of trivia, so each adds something the other lacks.

reasons.opus: Both involve quick reaction to slights and lingering over them, but pettish is childish sulking and peevishness while aggrieved is a sense of injustice that demands acknowledgment.

reasons.opus: Both involve childish sulking when crossed, but pettish centres on lingering peevish moods while immature is a broader childishness taking in blame-shifting, impatience and shirking.

reasons.opus: Both involve sexual activity outside commitment, but philandering is betrayal of a partner while promiscuity is having many casual partners. A single person can be promiscuous without cheating, and a philanderer may have just one affair.

reasons.opus: Both mean refusing to give ground, but pig-headed is an ego-driven refusal to update on evidence or argument, while unyielding is firmness against interpersonal pressure or pleading, which can be principled.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve refusing to bend, but pig-headed is stubborn resistance to argument and advice on positions held, while rigid is inflexible adherence to a fixed method or plan despite changing circumstances; each adds something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Both describe excessive, unrestrained consumption of food, but piggish also covers greedily grabbing goods and the largest share, while gluttonous centers on food and drink overindulgence.
reasons.opus: Both centre on overconsumption without restraint, but piggish stresses grabbing more than one's share of food or goods, while gluttonous is specifically excessive appetite for food and drink, not necessarily at others' expense.

reasons.opus: Both are about thinking past the present to possible outcomes, but prognosticating commits to specific forecasts while speculative explores many hypothetical possibilities without committing.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve looking ahead, but prognosticating is stating predictions about the future while proactive is acting in advance to prevent problems, so they are neighbouring but distinct concepts.

Both involve refusing to see one's own part and putting it on others, but projecting is attributing one's own hidden feelings or motives to others, while blame-shifting is deflecting fault for mishaps; each can occur without the other.
reasons.opus: Both deny one's own part and put it onto others, but projecting assigns one's feelings or motives to others, while blame-shifting assigns fault for outcomes; neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Prolific is about producing a large volume of creative work, while industrious is about habitual hard work and diligence; they relate (industry can drive output) but neither implies the other, and each has its own distinct focus.

Prolific is about the high volume and speed of creative output, while artistic is about a creative orientation and making beautiful things; they overlap in regularly producing work, but an artistic person need not be high-volume and a prolific person need not be artistic.

Both involve high output volume, but prolific is about producing written or artistic work, while frequent poster is about constant social participation and visibility in online spaces; neither implies the other.
Prominent is about public renown and influence, while well-connected is about having a network of personal contacts; they often go together but neither implies the other.
Betrothed (pledged to marry) and married (already wed) are adjacent but distinct marital statuses: one is a commitment to a future marriage, the other is the marriage itself.
Homophobia is one specific form of prejudice held and acted on personally, while promoting bigotry is actively advocating prejudice against any group; they overlap but neither implies the other.
Both involve hostility toward others, but promoting bigotry is advocacy of group-targeted prejudice, while malevolence is general ill will toward anyone, so each can occur without the other.

Both involve viewing groups as unequal, but promoting bigotry is actively advocating contempt or hostility toward a group, while elitism is a belief in the superiority of some and need not involve advocacy or hostility.
Promoting is about publicizing products or causes to a wide audience, while persuasive is about winning individuals over to a view or offer; they overlap in advocacy but neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve pushing one's offer or cause on others. Promoting is spreading the word and visibility, while persuasive is about winning agreement through argument, so each can exist without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve pushing a cause outward, but promoting is deliberate publicity for products or causes, while zealous is intense, crusading passion and distrust of coolness; neither implies the other.

Promoting is actively advertising products or causes to others, while frequent posting is high-volume participation in online spaces; they can co-occur, but neither implies the other and the cores differ.

Prompting is supplying cues or reminders so someone acts or speaks, while encouraging is backing someone's plans and urging them to aim higher; both nudge others toward action, but the means and aims differ.
Both guide others indirectly instead of giving answers, but prompting supplies cues so people act or speak, while socratic uses questions to lead people to their own insight.

Prompting is the specific act of giving cues or reminders to trigger action, while helpful is a broad disposition of caring and providing what others need; prompting could be one way of helping but the concepts are distinct.

Neuroticism is a broad trait covering anxiety, irritability, sadness, self-consciousness, impulsiveness and stress vulnerability, and bodily worry is only a narrow health-anxiety slice that the description doesn't even mention.

Both involve reading bodily twinges as grave threats, but the target is about health anxiety and bodily sensations while the other is a broader fear of mortality and death-related topics, so each has features the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both read every twinge as dire, but health worry centres on bodily symptoms while death-fear is a broader dread of mortality, funerals and the grave, so each can exist without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve worry, but the target is specifically health and bodily-sensation worry (hypochondriacal), while anxious is general worry and nervousness across any domain.

Both involve strain from sustained pressure, but burnout-proneness is a tendency toward depletion and exhaustion while stressed is a current state of tension and near-cracking; each lacks what the other adds.
reasons.opus: Both concern being overtaxed by sustained pressure, but burnout-proneness is a tendency toward depletion and exhaustion, while stressed is a current tense, overloaded state; each adds something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Both concern exhaustion from sustained pressure, but 'prone to burnout' is a susceptibility to becoming depleted while 'burned-out' is the established state with cynicism and detachment; each adds something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both centre on exhaustion from work stress, but the target is a tendency to run down under pressure, while the other is a present state that adds cynicism and loss of meaning.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve low energy and exhaustion, but burnout is depletion caused by sustained stress or workload, while lethargy is a habitual sluggishness that is not tied to pressure.

Both involve concern with social standing and keeping score, but comparing is measuring oneself against others and deriving self-worth from it, while status-seeking is pursuing signals of rank and admiration; either can occur without the other.
reasons.opus: Both centre on rank relative to others, but comparing is about measuring oneself and deriving self-worth, while status-seeking is about actively pursuing signals to be looked up to; each can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve self-worth tied to others, but comparing is a specific habit of measuring oneself against others, while insecurity is broader self-doubt, reassurance-seeking and criticism-sensitivity; neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve self-worth judged relative to others, but comparing is a habit of measurement that can end in feeling superior, while insecurity is chronic self-doubt that seeks reassurance; neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve measuring success by status and possessions, but comparing is about judging oneself against others across many domains, while materialism is a focus on wealth and goods and a rejection of the spiritual; neither implies the other.

Both involve measuring oneself against others, but comparing is a habit of self-assessment that sets one's sense of standing, while competitiveness is a drive to win and outperform; either can occur without the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve measuring oneself against others. Comparing is about deriving self-worth from where one stands, while competitive is about striving to win, so each can exist without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve inflated claims, but exaggeration is a general habit of overstating anything, whereas grandiosity is an inflated sense of one's own importance and abilities; each can occur without the other.
Both involve inflated speech, but exaggeration is about overstating facts and figures, while bombast is about grandiose, pompous style meant to impress; either can occur without the other.

Both involve inflating claims, but exaggeration is a general overstatement of events and numbers, while self-aggrandizing is specifically about inflating one's own importance; neither implies the other.
Both involve reaching for grander words, but exaggeration is overstating facts and events, while pretentiousness is putting on airs to seem cultured or important; each can occur without the other.
Both involve overstatement, but exaggeration is inflating facts, numbers and claims, while melodrama is theatrical emotional expression; each can occur without the other.
Both involve stating things that aren't accurate, but exaggeration inflates real events while confabulation invents details to fill knowledge gaps; neither implies the other.
Both involve habitual falling short, but 'prone to failure' is about unsuccessful outcomes while 'pathetic' adds feebleness and provoking contempt, and neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both describe habitually falling short, but prone to failure is about outcomes of attempts, while pathetic is feeble character and conduct that draws contempt. Each adds something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Prone to failure describes a pattern of actually falling short, while defeatist describes an expectation of failure and a habit of giving up; they are related, and defeatism can cause failure, but neither implies the other.

Both involve a pattern of falling short, but 'prone to failure' is about attempts routinely not succeeding at one's own goals, whereas 'unreliable' is about not following through on commitments to others; each can occur without the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve not delivering, but being prone to failure is about attempts falling short despite effort, while unreliability is about not following through on commitments to others; they are neighbouring concepts rather than the same one.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve repeated failure at tasks, but incompetence specifically means lacking skill as the cause, while prone to failure is about the outcome pattern, which could stem from bad luck, self-sabotage, or other causes.
reasons.opus: Both involve repeatedly failing. Incompetence stresses a lack of skill at doing tasks, while being prone to failure is a pattern of outcomes that could have other causes, such as overreaching or bad luck.

reasons.sonnet: Prone to failure is a pattern of attempts ending in failure, while languishing is a broader state of stagnation, aimlessness, disconnection and emptiness; they share some 'doing poorly' but neither implies the other.

Prone to failure is about habitually falling short in outcomes, while lazy is about avoiding effort; laziness can cause failure but they are different concepts, and a person can fail despite effort or succeed despite laziness.
Prone to failure is a general pattern of attempts ending in failure, whereas sloppy is a specific careless work style that can cause errors but doesn't necessarily mean failing overall.
One is a person's subjective tendency to feel excluded, the other is the objective social fact of being disliked and left out; they are related and may co-occur, but neither implies the other.

Both involve social pain, but feeling excluded from groups and plans is a different thing from craving company and lacking it; a person can feel left out while well-connected, or be lonely without being excluded.

One is a subjective tendency to feel excluded from groups, the other an objective lack of any social contacts or network; they are related around social disconnection but distinct, since a person can feel left out while well connected and be isolated without feeling it.

Both involve social distance, but feeling excluded when left out differs from the HEXACO social-introversion profile of self-perceived unpopularity, discomfort in the spotlight, declining invitations and low energy; they share only a partial core of feeling on the outside.

Both involve restlessness, but the target is restlessness triggered by confinement and lost autonomy, while the other is a general inability to settle even when nothing is wrong, so each adds something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both involve restlessness, but the target is a reaction to being constrained, while restless is a general inability to settle even when nothing is constraining.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve fear of not being wanted in relationships, but the target is a habitual feeling of rejection read from ordinary distance, while anxious-preoccupied attachment is a broader pattern of craving closeness and worrying about being valued less, and either can exist without the other.
reasons.opus: Both centre on insecurity about being valued by others, but anxious attachment is a craving for intimacy and closeness, while the target is reading ordinary distance as rejection; each can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve painful social disconnection, but feeling unwanted is a habit of interpreting distance as rejection, while loneliness is lacking company and missing people; either can occur without the other.

Both involve self-worth doubts and reading cues as confirmation, but feeling unwanted by others is about perceived rejection, while insecurity is broader self-doubt, inferiority and reassurance-seeking; neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve reading others' behaviour as proof of a negative belief about oneself. One centres on feeling rejected by others, the other on doubting one's own worth, so neither strictly implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both stem from insecurity about relationships, but one is a habit of feeling rejected and interpreting distance as being unwanted, while the other is a behavioral need for closeness and reassurance; neither implies the other.

Both involve strong emotional reactions to interpersonal events, but feeling chronically unwanted is a specific rejection-sensitivity, while emotional engagement is a broad intensity of response to slights and kindnesses alike.

Both involve awareness of being observed and judged, but the target is a constant unease about imagined scrutiny even when unobserved, while self-conscious is embarrassment and anxiety reacting to actual attention; each adds something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both centre on an uneasy awareness of being observed. The target is about imagined, constant scrutiny even when no one is looking, while self-conscious is embarrassment when people actually look, so each has something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve concern with others' imagined judgment, but one is a constant sense of being observed and the other is sensitivity to condemnation and ridicule that drives behavior; neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both centre on imagined observation and judgment by others, but feeling watched is a constant sense of being on display, while shame-proneness is a moral orientation in which fear of exposure governs conduct; each can exist without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve self-consciousness about others' judgment, but feeling watched is a sense of being observed and on display, while insecurity is doubting one's own worth and seeking reassurance; either can occur without the other.

Both involve attention on oneself, but feeling watched is an anxious perception of being observed, while self-effacing is a behavioral preference to avoid attention and be overlooked; neither implies the other.
Both concern the future, but forecasting is habitually predicting how events will unfold, while future-oriented is planning and weighing choices by their outcomes; neither implies the other.

Both involve looking ahead, but forecasting is habitually predicting how events will unfold, while proactive means anticipating needs and acting on them unprompted; the shared future orientation is the only overlap.

Both involve thinking about what might happen, but forecasting is habitually predicting how events will unfold, while speculative is open-ended conjecture and 'what if' exploration of possibilities without committing to predictions.
reasons.opus: Both involve thinking about possible future outcomes, but forecasting commits to predictions while speculation explores open hypotheticals without predicting, so neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve failing to act, but freezing is a pressure-triggered mental lock-up while helplessness is giving up when resources are missing and no workaround is seen; they differ in trigger and mechanism.

Both involve losing the thread mid-task or mid-sentence, but distractibility is attention being pulled away by stimuli or thoughts, while going blank is the thought simply dropping out; neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve losing the thread mid-task, but going blank is the thought dropping out on its own, while distractibility is attention being pulled away by stimuli, so each has something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve memory lapses, but going blank is losing one's thread mid-task or mid-sentence, while forgetful is failing to retain information like names, appointments and past events; neither implies the other.

Both involve asserting answers without adequate basis, but guessing is about filling gaps instead of checking or admitting ignorance, while overconfidence is about unwarranted certainty and never hedging; either can occur without the other.

Both can involve giving an answer without verification, but guessing is about bluffing instead of checking or admitting ignorance, while closure-seeking is a broader need for firm, settled answers and intolerance of ambiguity, so each adds something the other lacks.

Both involve working through disagreements, but hashing things out is about thorough, extended talking until settled, while win-win-seeking is about aiming for a settlement that fully meets both sides' needs; neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve staying with a disagreement until it is resolved. But hashing out is about thorough verbal discussion, while win-win-seeking is about holding out for an outcome that gives both sides everything, so neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve persistently working through problems until resolved, but one is talking disagreements out in conversation while the other is resolving logical contradictions in one's beliefs; neither implies the other.

Both involve engaging fully with difficult matters rather than avoiding them, but hashing things out is about extended verbal discussion until settled, while unflinching is about facing hard subjects head-on without necessarily talking at length.
reasons.opus: Both involve engaging fully with difficult matters rather than avoiding them, but hashing out is about talking things through to resolution while unflinching is about facing hard subjects directly; each can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve not stopping at the surface, but hashing things out is about talking a disagreement through to resolution in conversation, while thorough is about comprehensive analytical depth in any medium.

Hashing things out is about talking a problem through to resolution, while challenging is about pushing others to question assumptions; both involve engaged discussion but the core aims differ and neither implies the other.
Both involve drifting without purpose, but one is a specific online habit of aimless clicking and the other is a general lack of life direction; neither implies the other.
Both involve aimless drifting, but one is a specific online habit of purposeless browsing and the other is a broad state of stagnation and emptiness in life; neither implies the other.
Both involve heavy online time, but idle browsing is aimless, time-losing drifting, while plugged-in is being culturally fluent and up to date on feeds and trends; neither implies the other.
Both involve attention drifting, but idle browsing is aimless online wandering with lost time, while distractibility is attention being pulled off a task by any stimulus; neither implies the other.
Both involve resentful feelings toward others, but jealousy centers on fear of losing attention or affection to rivals, while envy centers on begrudging others' advantages or possessions.

Both involve envy of those who receive attention, but jealousy is about suspicion and resentment over rivals for others' affection, while vulnerable narcissism is a broader pattern of entitlement, hypersensitivity to slights, and brooding withdrawal.
Both involve resentment, but jealousy is about suspicion and envy toward rivals over others' attention, while aggrieved is about dwelling on perceived wrongs and unfairness; neighbouring concepts.
Insecurity (self-doubt, needing reassurance) is a common root of jealousy, but jealousy is specifically resentful suspicion toward rivals, so each has features the other lacks.

Both involve giving resources to others, but lending money casually without thought about repayment is a narrow, impulsive behavior, while generosity is a broad disposition of giving many kinds of resources, and each can occur without the other.
reasons.opus: Both centre on handing resources to others, but lending money casually can come from carelessness or poor boundaries rather than generosity, and generosity covers far more than lending money.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve loose, thoughtless handling of money, but lending money to others without expecting repayment is different from lavish spending on oneself; either can occur without the other.

Both describe deliberately telling falsehoods to mislead, but 'prone to lying' stresses habitual, casual lying about everything while 'deceitful' stresses intent to mislead and also includes fabrication and misrepresentation, so they differ slightly in emphasis.
reasons.opus: Both describe telling falsehoods to mislead. 'Prone to lying' stresses habitual frequency, while 'deceitful' stresses deliberate misrepresentation, so they differ only in emphasis.

reasons.sonnet: Both concern lack of honesty, but the target is habitual outright lying while the other describes strategic spin, omission and false confidence, which can occur without actual falsehoods.

Both involve stating falsehoods, but habitual lying is deliberate deception for convenience, whereas confabulation is filling knowledge gaps with plausible inventions, often without intent to deceive.
Habitual lying is one way of being untrustworthy, but untrustworthy also covers broken promises, leaked confidences and self-serving behavior, while a habitual liar need not do those things.

Both involve untruthfulness, but habitual lying about anything is broader and more deliberate, while intellectual dishonesty is specifically about distorting evidence and one's own findings, including self-deception, so each has features the other lacks.
Both involve saying wrong things, but misspeaking is a verbal slip where the wrong word comes out, while inaccuracy is getting facts and details wrong through misremembering and not noticing.
Both involve excess effort, but overexerting is about exceeding one's own limits and suffering for it, while overdiligent is about exceeding what the task requires; neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve excessive effort, but overexertion concerns exceeding one's own capacity at a personal cost, while overdiligence concerns exceeding what the task requires; either can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve being stretched past one's limits, but overexerting is a habitual behavior of pushing oneself too hard, while stressed is a strained state of tension and irritability; one can lead to the other without either implying it.

Both involve misrepresenting facts, but overstating is habitual exaggeration for emphasis that need not be intentional deception, while deceitfulness is deliberate lying and fabrication that need not involve inflation.

Both involve misrepresenting facts, but overstating is specifically inflating claims, while this dishonesty covers omission, false confidence and strategic framing; each includes things the other lacks, with overlap in projecting unwarranted certainty.

Both involve intrusive, repetitive thoughts that are hard to shake, but OCD adds compulsive behaviors, specific obsession themes, and awareness of irrationality, while rumination is general worry-circling without those rituals.
reasons.opus: Both centre on unwanted thoughts that keep returning, but OCD adds compulsive rituals and irrational fears, while rumination is replaying real problems without resolving them.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve repetitive, persistent thought returning to the same content, but rumination is worry-laden replaying of problems while obsessive is compulsive intense focus on details, and neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both describe thinking that keeps returning to the same content, but rumination is worried replaying of problems while obsessiveness is compulsive fixation on details, and either can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve getting stuck without progress, but rumination is repetitive worrying thoughts, while tunnel vision is rigid fixation on one approach and failure to reconsider assumptions.

Both involve self-doubt and second-guessing conclusions, but 'uncertain' is broader, adding hedging and hesitant expression, while the target focuses on reopening decisions and doubting one's own reasoning.
reasons.opus: Both centre on self-doubt and second-guessing. Self-questioning is the habit of reopening one's own decisions and reasoning, while uncertainty is an outward lack of conviction shown through hedging and hesitation, so each has a part the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve doubt around decisions, but self-questioning is habitual doubting and reopening of one's own judgments after the fact, while indecisiveness is inability to settle on a choice; either can occur without the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve doubt about one's choices, but self-questioning means reopening decisions already made, while indecisiveness means never reaching a decision at all.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve reconsidering one's own approach, but self-questioning is habitual self-doubt and second-guessing, while course-correcting is a deliberate, adaptive reassessment that leads to changing tack, so each has features the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both involve re-examining one's own reasoning and decisions. Self-questioning is a habitual, doubt-driven disposition, while course-correcting is a needs-triggered reassessment that leads to actually changing tack.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve habitual questioning, but one turns inward on one's own judgments and decisions while the other turns outward on claims and information, so they are neighbouring but distinct.

Both involve strong reactions to sensory stimuli like sudden noises, but sensory aversion is persistent irritation and discomfort across many sensations, whereas jumpiness is a startle and alertness response to sudden or unexpected events.

Both involve strong aversive reactions to unpleasant stimuli, but the target is sensitivity to everyday sensory input such as sounds, textures and glare, while squeamishness is revulsion at gory, rotten or depraved things; they overlap only in the general aversion.
Both can involve loud outbursts, but shrieking is a habit of piercing high-pitched vocalizing, while maniacal is a broader wild, frenzied, out-of-control manner that need not involve shrieking.
Both involve loud, heightened reactions, but shrieking is a specific vocal behavior while excitability is a general temperament of being easily worked up; neither implies the other.

Both involve constant preoccupation with one's own body, but one is fear of illness from bodily sensations while the other is fixation on weight, appearance and calories, so they share only the general focus on the body.

Both involve reacting strongly to sudden stimuli, but squealing is a vocal expression triggered by fear or excitement, while jumpiness is a nervous, easily startled temperament with no shrieking required.

Both involve disregarding others' boundaries and feeling entitled to intrude, but one is physical entry onto property and the other is prying into private affairs, so they are neighbouring distinct concepts.

Both involve habitually crossing boundaries, but trespassing is physically entering others' property while overstepping is exceeding one's authority or role; they share the boundary-crossing core but differ in domain.
Both involve intruding on others' boundaries, but trespassing is physical entry onto property while meddling is prying into and interfering with personal affairs.

Trespassing is a specific habit of entering others' property without permission, while rule-breaking is a general disregard for rules; trespassing is one possible instance but neither implies the other.

Recklessness is a disposition to ignore risk and costs, which can cause trouble, while being prone to trouble is about mishaps finding one regardless of cause; they are linked but neither implies the other.
Both involve inner experiences beyond ordinary perception, but one is having spontaneous visual imagery and the other is trusting non-rational knowing; neither implies the other.

Both involve visible reactions to hardship, but wailing is loud, open crying out of distress, while self-pitying is dwelling on one's unfair luck and seeking sympathy; either can occur without the other.
Both involve openly showing feelings, but wailing is specifically loud lamenting of distress, while expressive covers any emotion (joys, worries) and verbal openness; neither implies the other.

Both involve trying to win people over, but propagandist stresses one-sided, selective messaging for a cause, while persuasive is a general drive to change minds through argument, selling or bargaining, with no one-sidedness implied.

Both involve one-sided advocacy without balance, but the propagandist is defined by crafting persuasive one-sided messaging, while the partisan is defined by loyal side-taking and distrust of opponents; neither implies the other.

Both involve selectively presenting favorable information and omitting inconvenient points, but propagandist is about promoting a cause through one-sided messaging while this 'dishonest' also covers false confidence and hiding limitations, so each adds something the other lacks.

Both involve one-sided advocacy, but propagandist is deliberate selective messaging for a cause, while opinionated is holding and voicing strong views on everything without necessarily suppressing contrary evidence.

Both involve one-sided handling of evidence favoring a desired conclusion, but the propagandist does it outwardly to persuade others, while the motivated reasoner does it inwardly and ends up deceiving themselves.

Both involve persuasion, but propagandist is about one-sided promotion of a cause that omits counterpoints, while rhetorical is about using persuasive techniques and figures of speech, which need not be one-sided or tied to a cause.

Both involve one-sidedness in what gets heard, but the propagandist actively pushes a cause with selective messaging while the exclusionary simply leaves out non-mainstream voices without promoting anything.

Both involve active communication, but propagating is a duty-driven spreading of particular ideas to as many people as possible, while frequent posting is high-volume participation and visibility on every topic, so each has features the other lacks.

Both involve respectable bearing in company, but proper is about correct manners and conformity to expectations, while dignified is about poise, self-respect and avoiding looking ridiculous; neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both concern decorous public bearing, but proper is about correct manners and conforming to expected respectability, while dignified is about poise, composure and self-respect; each can exist without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both concern courteous, well-mannered behavior, but 'proper' stresses decorum and respectability while 'polite' stresses civil everyday courtesies; each can exist without the other.
reasons.opus: Both are about good manners, but proper stresses decorum and respectability in all conduct, while polite is about civil courtesies toward others; they share a core and each adds something.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve conforming to conduct norms, but 'proper' is about correct manners and decorum while 'well-behaved' as described is about rule-abiding, orderly avoidance of mischief and disapproval of troublemakers; each adds something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both are about correct, orderly conduct, but proper stresses decorum and respectability, while well-behaved stresses avoiding pranks, mischief and rule-bending. A persona can have either without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve respectable, unshocking conduct, but proper is about correct manners and decorum while staid adds settled, conservative, controversy-avoiding temperament; each can exist without the other.
reasons.opus: Both centre on respectability, but proper is about correct manners and decorous conduct, while staid is about safe opinions and avoiding controversy; each adds something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve correctness and decorum, but 'proper' is about manners and respectable conduct generally, while 'formal' is about language register and tone in official contexts; each can exist without the other.
reasons.opus: Both share a core of correctness and dignified restraint, but proper is about overall decorous conduct and manners, while formal is specifically about a professional register of language; each can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both concern lacking wealth, but propertyless means owning nothing at all, while poor means low income and hardship, and a poor person may own some things while a propertyless person need not suffer deprivation.
reasons.opus: Both centre on owning almost nothing, but propertyless is about total absence of ownership, while poor adds low income and material deprivation, and a poor person may still own a few things.

reasons.sonnet: Propertyless is about owning nothing, whereas spartan is a deliberate choice of plain, austere living and disdain for luxury; they can occur separately (a wealthy spartan, or an involuntarily propertyless person).

Both concern the future, but prophetic means confidently foretelling specific coming events, while futuristic means emphasizing emerging trends and next-generation approaches; neither implies the other.
Both concern the future, but prophetic is about foretelling events with confident vision, while future-oriented is about planning and weighing choices by where they lead; neither implies the other.

Both involve looking ahead to the future, but prophetic is foretelling events with confidence, while proactive is anticipating needs and acting on them unprompted; one is about speech and prediction, the other about action.

Both concern thinking or speaking about the future, but prophetic means confidently foretelling a specific outcome, while speculative means tentatively exploring multiple hypothetical possibilities without confidence.

Both involve calming conflict, but propitiating is appeasing an angry person with concessions, while conciliatory is working to make peace and find common ground between sides, so each adds something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both aim to calm conflict and restore goodwill, but propitiating is appeasing an angry party with concessions, while conciliatory is broader peacemaking and finding common ground, including between other sides.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve conceding to keep the peace, but propitiating is specifically soothing angry or offended people, while accommodating is a general readiness to adjust to others' needs without needing anger present.
reasons.opus: Both involve conceding to others to keep peace. Propitiating targets angry people specifically, using warm words. Accommodating is a general flexibility to meet needs, so neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve keeping peace and avoiding conflict, but propitiating is specifically soothing angry or offended people with concessions, while agreeable is a broader general disposition toward harmony and cooperation.
reasons.opus: Both center on preserving harmony and defusing conflict. Propitiating is specifically placating angry people with concessions, while agreeable is a broader cooperative disposition, so they overlap but neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve defusing conflict and conciliation, but propitiating is actively soothing angry people with concessions, while HEXACO agreeableness is forgiving, lenient, cooperative and even-tempered, so each includes things the other lacks.

Both aim to win favor and smooth over tension, but propitiating specifically calms anger through concessions and warm words, while flattering is insincere praise used in any situation, so each has something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both seek to win favor and smooth tension, but propitiating means appeasing someone's anger with concessions, while flattering means insincere praise in general. Each can happen without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Propitiating is actively appeasing angry people with concessions to head off hostility, while forgiving is pardoning wrongs and letting go of grudges; both concern conflict and reconciliation but they are different behaviors.

Both involve avoiding conflict through concessions, but propitiating is actively soothing angry people while peaceful is a general nonviolent, compromising approach; each has something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both lean toward conciliation and compromise over conflict, but propitiating is actively appeasing someone who is already angry, while peaceful is a general nonviolent way of pursuing one's aims; each can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both concern heeding risk, but proportionate caution is about calibrating care to risk size (including moving freely when stakes are small), while prudent is about foresight and heeding risks, so each adds something the other lacks.

Proportionate caution is about scaling precautions to the real size of risk, while data-driven is about relying on quantitative evidence over anecdotes; they are related, since base rates can inform risk sizing, but neither implies the other.

Both concern care about risk, but proportionate caution calibrates precaution to stakes (and moves freely when risks are small), while cautious is a general tendency to hold back under uncertainty, so each lacks something the other has.

Both involve authoritative rule-setting, but proscriptive forbids what must not be done while prescriptive dictates what must be done, so they are neighbouring distinct concepts rather than the same quality at opposite ends.

reasons.sonnet: Purposive is about directing actions toward chosen goals, while focused is about sustaining attention against distractions on a task; they are related but concern different things (goal direction vs. attentional control).

reasons.opus: Both concern goal-directed behaviour, but purposive is about acting with definite intent toward chosen aims, while self-disciplined is about resisting impulses to stick to commitments; each can exist without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve goal-directed action, but purposive is about keeping each step aimed at chosen goals, while strategic adds long-term planning, forgoing short-term wins and keeping fallbacks; neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both aim actions at goals, but purposive is about deliberate intent toward chosen goals, while strategic adds long-term planning, sacrificing short-term wins, and fallbacks; one can be purposive without strategic foresight and vice versa.

reasons.sonnet: Purposive is about directing actions toward clearly chosen goals, while persevering is about persisting through setbacks to finish a hard goal; both involve goal pursuit, but neither implies the other.

reasons.opus: Both involve putting on airs and looking down on others. Purse-proud is specifically about wealth, while pretentious is about seeming cultured or important, so each has something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve pride and haughtiness, but purse-proud is specifically wealth-based condescension, while Leo is a broad royal persona that is warm, generous and dignified, with pride only one part.

reasons.opus: Both involve a superior attitude toward others. Purse-proud is specifically wealth-based disdain and display, while condescending is patronizing talk-down based on intellect or morals, so each adds something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Purse-proud is a haughty, condescending attitude about one's wealth, while upper-class describes social background and polish; they are related but neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve self-serving manipulation, but the target is specifically covert steering while feigning neutrality, whereas the other is a broader mix of flattery, rule-breaking, greed and entitlement.

Both involve an orientation toward gain, but one is steering recommendations toward profit and sales, while the other is doing work only for external rewards of any kind; neither implies the other.

Both involve forcefully pressing a point repeatedly, but pushy moralizing is specifically about imposing moral verdicts on others, while emphatic is a general forceful style of expression on any topic.

Both involve an unpleasant interpersonal style and quickness to judge, but pushy moralizing is about insistently imposing moral views, while harshness is about severity and cutting delivery, and neither implies the other.

Both involve certainty that one's own view is right, but pushy moralizing is about repeatedly lecturing others on morality, while exclusivism is about dismissing rival views as errors, with no implied pressing or moral lecturing.

Both involve urgency and pushing for speed, but impatience is an internal restlessness and visible frustration, while pressuring others is actively leaning on them until they give way; each can occur without the other.
Both involve forceful pushing to get one's way, but pressuring others is about urging speed or compliance, while aggression is about confrontation and rejecting compromise; neither implies the other.

Both involve asserting influence over others, but pressuring is coercive urging toward faster action or compliance, while dominance is broader control and steering of conversations without necessarily applying pressure.

Both involve coercive behavior toward others, but pressuring is about pushing for speed or compliance, while bullying is about picking on the weak through mockery and intimidation; each includes elements the other lacks.

Both prioritize safety and avoiding harm, but the target is specifically about teenagers as the top-ranked concern, while 'harmless' is a general harm-avoidance toward everyone, so they overlap without either implying the other.

Both involve faking feelings or qualities one lacks to impress others; 'putter-on' stresses affected airs of importance or sophistication, while 'phony' is a broader false self-presentation including fake warmth and expertise.
reasons.opus: Both describe putting on a false show that one doesn't genuinely feel. The putter-on is a narrower case focused on affected airs of importance, while the phony covers fake warmth or expertise and a false self generally.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve affecting airs of importance or sophistication to impress, but 'putter-on' is broader (any feigned feeling or manner) while 'pretentious' adds name-dropping, showy vocabulary and disdain for plain tastes.
reasons.opus: Both centre on affecting airs of importance or sophistication to impress. Putter-on also covers feigned feelings in general, while pretentious stresses cultural show-off and looking down on plain tastes, so they differ mainly in emphasis.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve putting on a front for an audience, but the target is affecting airs of importance or sophistication, while the other is behaving correctly only under observation and cheating when unobserved; each adds something the other lacks.

Both involve putting on a false front for an audience, but putter-on stresses affecting feelings or airs of importance one lacks, while performative stresses constant audience-reading and adjusting opinions and stories; each adds something the other lacks.

Both make a person unpredictable and hard to read, but puzzling is about opaque, inconsistent signals, while erratic is about abrupt unexplained shifts in tone and view; either can occur without the other.
reasons.opus: Both leave others unable to predict what comes next, but puzzling is about being hard to read while erratic is about abrupt inconsistent switching, and each can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve being hard for others to understand, but puzzling is about inconsistent signals that leave others unable to read one's wants or actions, while cryptic is about deliberately obscure communication; neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both leave others unable to work out meaning, but puzzling is an overall, not necessarily deliberate, inscrutability of wants, feelings and actions, while cryptic is a deliberately enigmatic way of communicating.

reasons.sonnet: Both leave others unable to read the person, but puzzling comes from signals that don't add up, while opaque is deliberately withholding reasoning and information; each can occur without the other.
reasons.opus: Both leave others unable to read the person, but puzzling comes from contradictory signals while opaque comes from deliberately withholding information, so neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve following established ways of doing things, but 'pythonic' is specific to Python idioms and readability, while 'conventional' is a general disposition of distrusting originality.

Both involve faking expertise or sincerity, but quack is specifically fraudulent medical/expert claims sold for gain, while phony is a broader false self-presentation including feigned warmth; neither implies the other.
Quackery is deliberate fraud about one's credentials and cures, while overconfidence is sincere, unjustified certainty; they share only the surface of unwarranted confidence.

Both involve deceptive presentation and false confidence, but quackery is specifically faking expert credentials and selling false cures, while this dishonesty is a broader pattern of spin and omission without fake expertise.

Quackery is a specific kind of deception (faking expertise and selling false cures), while deceitful is general lying and misrepresentation; they share deception but quack adds fake credentials and selling, and deceitful covers much more.
Both involve the past, but quaint is an old-fashioned style and manner, while nostalgic is a sentimental fondness for and preference for earlier times; either can exist without the other.
reasons.opus: Both centre on the past, but quaint is an old-fashioned manner and style, while nostalgic is a fond preference for past eras; either can exist without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve old-world manners and refinement, but quaint is a charming old-fashioned style while shabby-genteel is about fallen fortunes and keeping up genteel appearances in poverty.
Quaint is about a charmingly old-fashioned style and manner, while old money is about inherited generational wealth and its associated status; they may co-occur but are different concepts.
Both lean toward the old rather than the new, but quaint is a charming old-fashioned style and manner, while traditional is a preference for established, proven methods; neither implies the other.
reasons.opus: Both lean toward the old, but quaint is a charming old-fashioned style and manner, while traditional is a preference for proven, established methods over new ones; each can exist without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Quaker is a specific religious affiliation, while religious describes a general disposition of reasoning from faith; Quakerism is one instance of religiousness, but being Quaker doesn't require the described scripture-based reasoning, and religious people are mostly not Quakers.

Both concern formal schooling, but 'qualified' means having the specific credentials a field requires, while 'educated' means having completed college or graduate study in general; one can be educated without being qualified for a particular field, and qualified without a college degree.
reasons.opus: Both involve formal training, but being qualified means meeting a field's specific requirements, which need not include a degree, while being educated means having a college background, which need not qualify one for any particular field.

reasons.sonnet: Qualified is about holding formal credentials or training, while specialist is about deep domain expertise and mastery; they share a link to competence but neither implies the other.

Both involve demanding behavior toward others, but quarter-decker is about rigid rank, regulation, and deference, while strict is about high standards, results, and tough-love pushing; they share a core of severity but each adds something distinct.

Both involve dominating others, but quarter-decker is about enforcing rigid rank, regulation and deference, while controlling is about needing the final say and monitoring others' movements and associations; each adds something the other lacks.

Both involve rigid, rank-based demands for obedience and strict correction of lapses, but the target is a general disciplinarian focused on order, dress and deference, while the other is a parenting style centered on children's obedience and punishment of self-will.
Quarter-decker is about imposing rigid discipline and rank on others, while rule-abiding is about personally following rules; they share a rule-focused core but neither implies the other.

Both concern hierarchy and rules, but the quarter-decker imposes strict discipline on others from a position of authority while the obedient person submits to authority, so they are neighbouring but distinct concepts.

Both involve severity toward others, but quarter-decker is about rigid rank-based discipline and enforcing regulations, while harsh is about heavy-handed judgment and cutting bluntness; neither implies the other.

reasons.opus: Both describe a regal bearing and being used to command, but queening stresses imperious demands for deference, while Leo adds warmth, generosity and a love of the limelight.

reasons.opus: Both centre on expecting others to serve or defer as one's due, but queening adds commanding, regal bearing while entitled adds resentment when privileges are withheld, so neither implies the other.

reasons.opus: Both rest on an inflated sense of superiority, but queening is about commanding others and expecting deference, while grandiosity is about exaggerated claims of one's own greatness; neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve a superior attitude toward others, but queening is imperious commanding and expecting deference, while arrogance is overconfidence and condescension about one's abilities and knowledge; each can occur without the other.
reasons.opus: Both involve a sense of superiority, but queening is commanding others and expecting service and deference, while arrogant is overconfidence in one's own knowledge and condescension, so each has elements the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve taking charge over others, but queening is imperious, entitled expectation of deference and service, while dominant is assertive control and steering of discussions, which need not be haughty or entitled.
reasons.opus: Both involve taking control and directing others. Queening adds regal entitlement and an expectation of deference, while dominant is assertive steering of conversations without the haughty air, so each has something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve commanding, authoritative language, but queening is about imperious entitlement and expecting deference, while prescriptive is about laying down specific rules and instructions, so each lacks what the other adds.
reasons.opus: Both involve issuing authoritative commands, but queening centres on regal entitlement and expecting deference, while prescriptive centres on laying down specific rules and instructions, and neither implies the other.

Quenchless is about insatiable, never-satisfied craving, while hedonistic is about prioritizing pleasure over responsibilities; they share a pleasure-seeking flavor but neither implies the other.
Quenchless is a general insatiability across any appetite, while lustful is strong sexual desire specifically; they share the idea of intense craving but neither implies the other.

reasons.opus: Both are disagreeable fault-finding, but querulousness is habitual peevish complaining about everything, while quarrelsomeness centres on grudges, stubborn arguing and quick anger at people.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve complaining about trivial matters, but querulous is habitual peevish fault-finding about everything, while petty is blowing minor slights out of proportion (including grudges), so each has something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both involve airing grievances, but querulousness is habitual complaining about everything, while pettiness is blowing trivial slights out of proportion, so each can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve dissatisfaction, but querulous is the outward habit of peevish complaining and fault-finding, while discontented is an inner dissatisfaction with one's life that need not be voiced.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve speed in replying, but quick-fire is about brief, rapid-succession delivery without elaboration, while quick-witted is about sharp mental acuity and apt replies; neither implies the other.

reasons.opus: Both involve acting without lengthy deliberation, but quick to act is prompt decisiveness in response to situations or requests, while impulsive is being driven by urges with disregard for consequences.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve acting directly without much deliberation, but 'quick to act' is about speed and committing without second-guessing, while 'tactical' is about narrow, immediate problem-solving with no larger plan; neither implies the other.

reasons.opus: Both involve dealing with things at once, but quick to act is about decisiveness without deliberating, while hurried is about treating every matter as urgent, so each adds something the other lacks.

reasons.opus: Both involve urgency and avoiding lengthy deliberation, but impatience adds frustration and pressing others, while quick action is about decisive commitment without the emotional chafing.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve acting without delay, but 'bold' adds optimism about risk and self-trust over experts, while 'quick to act' is only about speed of commitment without deliberation.
reasons.opus: Both involve acting now without waiting. Bold adds risk-taking and self-trust, while quick to act is about speed and decisiveness even on safe matters, so they share a core but neither implies the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve owning one's mistakes, but quick apologizing centers on immediate, frequent saying sorry (even in small matters), while accountability centers on proportionate ownership and fixing things, with no emphasis on apologizing; each adds something the other lacks.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve hasty negative judgments of others without much consideration, but blame-assigning is specifically about attributing fault or responsibility, while judgmental is broader criticism of choices and circumstances, so each adds something the other lacks.
reasons.opus: Both involve hasty negative verdicts about others. Blaming is specifically about deciding who caused a fault, while judgmentalness is broader harsh appraisal of people's choices, so each can occur without the other.

reasons.sonnet: Both involve hostility toward others, but quick blame-pinning is about hastily attributing fault, while quarrelsomeness is about grudges, argumentativeness and anger; they overlap only in being critical of others' faults.

reasons.opus: Both centre on easily felt embarrassment that shows as reddening. reasons.sonnet: Quick to blush is about visible embarrassment at small slips or compliments, while timid is about fearfulness and hanging back from the unfamiliar; both involve shyness but neither implies the other.

reasons.opus: Both concern even temper, but recovering quickly after a flare is different from rarely being worked up in the first place.

reasons.opus: Quick recovery from anger is one narrow part of broad emotional stability, which also covers being slow to anger, optimism, social ease and steadiness under stress, so one is a facet of the other.

reasons.sonnet: Quick to cool off is about anger fading soon after a flare-up, while composed is about steady calm and no nervous energy generally; they are neighbours in the area of emotional steadiness but not the same thing.

Both involve picking up on subtle social cues, but one is accurate reading of the room's mood while the other is suspicious interpretation of cues as disloyalty; different concepts that are neighbours.
